                                 HeapNumber per call at a non-inlined call site (measured 16 B/op under
                                 --no-turbo-inlining) -- use `totalInto` on a render path.
- totalInto(out, w?) -> 1        COLD, O(B+1), 0 B/call with w omitted or integral, at every inlining state
                                 (1.12.0; a FRACTIONAL w boxes 16 B as the call argument at a non-inlined
                                 site -- measured under --no-turbo-inlining). The 0-alloc render
                                 sibling of total(): writes total(w) into out[0] (Object.is-identical, the
                                 same live-pane loop) and returns 1. The S1 / S2 COLD-reader contract (parity
                                 with SlidingHyperLogLog.countInto): a non-Float64Array out throws TypeError
                                 (intrinsic tag), out.length < 1 throws RangeError (intrinsic length, read
                                 ONCE); out is untouched on a throw. A bad w writes out[0] = NaN and returns 1
                                 (checked before the unset return); an unset instance writes 0.
- estimateInto(keys, out, w?)    COLD, 0 B/op. The batch reader: keys / out caller-owned Float64Arrays
  -> number                      (out.length >= keys.length, else a tagged Type/RangeError BEFORE any
                                 write -- the container-type contract). Writes out[j] = estimate(keys[j], w)
                                 for each key (NaN for an out-of-domain key, 0 for an unseen valid key /
                                 empty window; a bad w fills every out[j] with NaN), returns keys.length. No
                                 computed double crosses a non-inlined call, so it stays 0 B/op where scalar
                                 estimate boxes a ~16 B HeapNumber for a count >= 2^31 (the F6 render path).
                                 keys and out MAY be the SAME array (slot j read then written before j+1) but
                                 must NOT PARTIALLY OVERLAP (an aliased non-zero offset gives wrong results).
- advance(now) -> this           Move the window's reference time to `now` WITHOUT adding (the R11 idle
                                 slide, ADR 0009): rotate + clear stale panes via the private _advance so
                                 an idle stream slides to empty (estimate 0). EXPLICIT-time ONLY (count-
                                 locked throws, unset locks EXPLICIT + anchors), monotone; bounded
                                 (<= B+1 clears), 0 B/op.
- advanceFrom(buf, i) -> this    The ZERO-BOX sibling of advance(now): `now = buf[i]` read UNBOXED (needs
                                 `i < buf.length`), same rotate body, EXPLICIT-only.
- clear() -> this                0-alloc reset (reuse the arrays; unlocks the mode).
- d / w / panes / W / seed / conservative / saturated / epsilon / delta / mode / lastNow / bytes
                                 Getters: the shape, the seed / mode knobs, the saturation honesty flag,
                                 the theoretical error e/w and failure e^-d, the locked mode, the last
                                 applied time, the fixed memory figure.

Windowed-frequency contract (the honesty anchor): the witness drives against an EXACT per-key ring oracle
and gates the ONE-SIDED bound true(W) <= est <= true(W+W/B) + epsilon*N on 100% of >= 2000 queries across
>= 4 (W, eps) pairs + a churny key stream + advance-empties. Negative controls rejected by the same gate: a
DROP-OLDEST-PANE variant (under-counts -> breaks the lower bound est >= true(W)) and a MIN-THEN-SUM variant
(min over rows per pane, then sum -> wrong). Memory ~ (B+1) * d * w * 4 B + paneEnd +
a per-pane Float64 total (`_paneTotal`, +(B+1)*8 B, the exact `total()` N) + scratch; the default `new
SlidingCountMin(60000)` is 338468 B (was 338204 B before `total`), never grows. ADR 0010 records the B+1 / keep-oldest one-sided-bound rationale, the rejected ECM-
sketch alternative, the absolute pane alignment, sum-then-min, per-pane conservative update, Uint32
saturation + `saturated`, the W-not-capped resolution, and the lite-sketch byte-parity note.

## DecayedReservoir (ADR 0011)

A recency-biased fixed-k SAMPLE of ACTUAL stream values -- the "give me k real recent items" member.
Where the other members each answer ONE pre-decided question (a count, a distinct, a quantile, a
frequency), a reservoir hands the caller `k` retained values from which they compute ANYTHING (any
quantile, any custom function), approximately. The sampling complement to `ForwardDecay`: FD gives
decayed AGGREGATES exactly (two scalars), DecayedReservoir gives a decayed SAMPLE (k slots). It is the
SAMPLE corner on the time axis.

Algorithm (ADR 0011): Efraimidis-Spirakis A-Res weighted reservoir sampling (Efraimidis-Spirakis,
"Weighted random sampling with a reservoir", 2006) with FORWARD-DECAY weights (Cormode et al., ICDE
2009 -- the same decay model as `ForwardDecay`). Each accepted item draws ONE uniform u in (0, 1) from
a seeded xorshift32 (the exact `HeavyKeeper` derivation, so seed=0 is a valid distinct seed) and forms
an A-Res key. The textbook key is `u^(1/w)` with weight `w = exp(lambda*(t - L))`; DecayedReservoir
works it in LOG SPACE -- `key = log(u) * exp(-lambda*(t - L)) * _scale` -- which is numerically STABLE
(`exp(-lambda*age)` underflows to 0 gracefully as age grows, instead of `exp(+...)` overflowing to
Inf). The k highest keys are kept in an intrusive size-k MIN-FOREST (design-parity with `HeavyKeeper` /
lite-o1 `FreqO1`, inlined -- never a dep): a new item whose key beats the forest root replaces it and
sifts down. Because recent items get keys nearer 0 (the top), they are more likely retained -- the
decay bias. The value column stores the payload alongside its key.

Landmark rebase (order-preserving, the key subtlety): as `t` advances from the landmark `L`,
`exp(-lambda*(t - L))` shrinks toward 0. When `lambda*(t - L)` exceeds `DR_EXP_CAP = 40` the landmark
rebases to `t` and a single scalar `_scale` absorbs the common factor -- this multiplies EVERY stored
key by the same positive constant, a MONOTONE transform, so the retained-set membership and the forest
order are UNCHANGED (no per-slot sweep; 0 B/op). A very large idle gap then a resume is capped at
`DR_F_CAP = 700` on the rebase-factor argument so a key can never underflow to -0 and tie the whole
forest (the ADWIN/FD/SLD overflow lesson, on the sampling axis). Because decay is applied at INSERT
and membership is fixed thereafter, an idle stream correctly HOLDS its last decayed sample -- there is
nothing to "slide to empty", so (like `ForwardDecay`) DecayedReservoir has NO `advance()`.

Constructor: `new DecayedReservoir(k, halfLife, options?)` where `k` is a positive integer (the sample
size, a positive integer <= 2^24 -- DR_K_MAX, ~256 MB at 16 B/slot; a bigger k throws a tagged
RangeError BEFORE allocation instead of a lazy multi-GB over-commit, F11), `halfLife` a finite number
> 0 (`lambda = ln2 / halfLife`), options = { seed (uint32, default 0x9e3779b1; seed=0 valid, guarded
as `undefined`) }. A bad k / halfLife / seed / option throws [lite-adaptive] at the ctor door BEFORE
any allocation.

- add(now?, value?) -> this      HOT, amortized 0 B/op incl. the PRNG draw + forest sift + rebase.
                                 EXPLICIT mode: a finite, non-decreasing `now`. COUNT mode:
                                 add(undefined, value) auto-ticks. The mode LOCKS at the first add (a
                                 switch throws). `value` is ANY finite real (signed OK), default 1.
                                 Value + now + mode are validated FIRST -- a reject is a byte-identical
                                 no-op that does NOT advance the PRNG or the landmark.
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this        HOT, 0 B/op ZERO-BOX stride-2: now = buf[i], value = buf[i+1] read
                                 UNBOXED from a packed [now, value] Float64Array. EXPLICIT-time only.
                                 Same validation + body as add.
- sampleInto(buf) -> number      COLD, 0 alloc. Copy the current retained VALUES into a caller
                                 Float64Array (length must be >= k, else throws); returns the count
                                 written (`size`, <= k). Order is heap order, NOT sorted.
- forEach(fn) -> void            Alloc-free iteration over the current sample: fn(value). A non-function
                                 fn throws [lite-adaptive] before iteration.
- clear() -> this                0-alloc reset (reuse both columns; unlock the mode; replay the PRNG
                                 from its seeded initial state -- a cleared reservoir replays identically).
- k / halfLife / lambda / seed / size / mode / bytes   Getters: the sample size, the decay knob,
                                 ln2/halfLife, the PRNG seed, the live sample size, the locked mode, and
                                 the fixed memory figure (`k * 16 + 64` bytes: two Float64 columns + scalars).

Recency-sample contract (the honesty anchor): the witness drives an evolving stream over many
independent seeds and gates that the sample's empirical INCLUSION RATE as a function of item AGE
decays as `exp(-lambda*age)` (recent items over-represented by exactly the decay factor), within a
stated statistical band. Negative controls REJECTED by the witness: a NO-DECAY reservoir (a plain
uniform draw -> flat inclusion rate, rejected by the slope fit) and a NO-FOREST reservoir (keep the
first k forever -> recent items never sampled, rejected because its newest-age inclusion rate is ~0).
A long-idle-then-resume lane asserts the sample stays
well-defined (no NaN, no ambiguous ties, membership deterministic across seeds). ADR 0011 records the
A-Res + log-space-forward-decay-key choice, the order-preserving-rebase proof, the seeded-PRNG choice,
the advance()-excluded rationale, the raw-sample-only surface, the min-forest reuse, and the rejected
alternatives (A-ExpJ skip-sampling; a hard-window sample; bundled convenience aggregates).

## SlidingAggregate (ADR 0012)

EXACT windowed count / sum / mean / min / max over the covered span [w, w+W/B] (which always CONTAINS the
last w), in FIXED preallocated space -- the
aggregate the rest of the family could not give. ExponentialHistogram's `sum()` is bounded by the oldest
straddling bucket's POPULATION (2^Lmax / 2), not its value mass, so on a skewed value stream it fails
(F17: worst 15.8% heavy tail, ~2504% on a spike); SlidingDDSketch answers quantiles, SlidingCountMin
per-key counts. SlidingAggregate is the EXACT-AGGREGATE corner on the time axis.

Window model (ADR 0012): B+1 preallocated panes of width W/B (the SlidingCountMin ring, COPIED verbatim
-- never a shared helper, so SCM's bytes and behavior cannot move), held in a ring. Per-pane state is
stride 5 in one Float64Array: `[count, sum, kcomp, min, max]`. add() folds into the CURRENT pane
(count += 1; a branch-free Kahan compensated sum `y = v - c; t = s + y; c = (t - s) - y; s = t`; min /
max by `<` / `>`), rotating to the next pane and CLEARING it to identity sentinels (count/sum/kcomp 0,
min +Infinity, max -Infinity -- NEVER fill(0) over the stride, or an all-positive window would read
min 0) as `now` crosses a pane boundary. A `now` jump of k panes clears min(k, B+1) panes, never loops k
(the SlidingCountMin bounded-rotation discipline). The query merges the LIVE, non-empty panes (paneEnd >
now - w, INCLUDING the straddling oldest pane) with Neumaier over the terms `{s_p, -c_p}`. The straddling
oldest pane is KEPT, so the covered span is [w, w + W/B]: always the FULL window, over-covered by at most
one pane width W/B and NEVER under-covered (dropping it would under-cover [w - W/B, w)).

Guarantee over the covered span [w, w + W/B], u = 2^-53:
- count, min and max are BIT-EXACT (the sign of a zero extreme is unspecified);
- `|sum - exact| <= (4u + O(N u^2)) * sum|v|` -- Kahan per pane contributes 2u (Higham ASNA eq. 4.8), the
  Neumaier merge over the 2(B+1) terms adds 2u. A 2u bound is NOT provable for this merge (even a one-pane
  window pays Kahan's 2u plus the final s + c rounding);
- `mean = sum / count` (one more rounding). Rejected: plain += (loses every 1.0 behind a 2^53); per-pane
  offset-centring (an extra hot field + a re-centre branch, and it still needs compensation).

Value domain: `value` is REQUIRED (no default of 1 -- a forgotten latency must fail closed). A finite
real with |value| <= 1e150 (SA_X_MAX, the same cap as DD_X_MAX), so |sum| <= n * 1e150 stays finite for
any physically reachable n and every Kahan / Neumaier intermediate stays finite. A non-number / NaN /
+-Infinity / over-cap value throws TypeError [lite-adaptive] value-first (a byte-identical no-op).

Time model: EXPLICIT (a monotone `now`) or COUNT mode (add(undefined, value)); the mode locks at the
first add and a switch throws. addFrom / advance / advanceFrom are EXPLICIT-only (ADR 0009). The rotate /
anchor helpers take NO argument and read `this._now`, so no epoch-ms double crosses a non-inlined call --
gated by a rotate-every-add epoch-clock lane. (In 1.10.0 SlidingCountMin and SlidingDDSketch adopted the
same argument-free _advance() / _anchor() reading this._now, so their per-rotation epoch cost is 0 B/op too.)

Precision domain (ADR 0012, amended by QA190): exact containment needs ulp(now) << pw. (1) pw = W / panes
must be a NORMAL double (>= 2^-1022, SA_MIN_NORMAL): a subnormal pw loses significand bits so (B+1)*pw can
fall below W and the ring under-covers -- the ctor throws [lite-adaptive] before allocating. (2) |now| (and
the count-mode tick) must be <= pw * 2^42 (SA_CLOCK_SPAN): at the bound ulp(now) <= pw * 2^-10 so the grid
line (floor(now/pw)+1)*pw still CONTAINS the true window; past it the window collapses (QA190 F1) or
under-covers (F2). add / addFrom / advance / advanceFrom reject a larger clock with RangeError
[lite-adaptive] BEFORE any state write (one field compare `!(t <= nowMax && t >= -nowMax)`, nowMax = pw *
2^42 precomputed in the ctor) -- rebase the clock (performance.now(), or subtract an epoch) or use a larger
W. Pane ends are computed by multiplication from the grid index ((k+1)*pw), not an accumulating E += pw that
drifts near the edge. Generous for real clocks: epoch-ms (W=1000, B=32) allows |now| <= 1.37e14, epoch-us
(W=1e6) <= 1.37e17, performance.now() (W=16) <= 2.2e12 ms.

Constructor: `new SlidingAggregate(W, options?)` where options = { panes (B; an integer in [2, 1024],
default 32 -- the ring holds B+1) }. A bad W / panes / option throws [lite-adaptive] at the ctor door
BEFORE any allocation; a W too small for panes (W / panes underflows to 0), or a W / panes that is a
SUBNORMAL double, throws before allocation.

- add(now, value) -> this        HOT, 0 B/op incl. pane rotate + clear. EXPLICIT (finite, non-decreasing
                                 `now`) or COUNT (add(undefined, value), auto-tick). value REQUIRED,
                                 finite, |value| <= 1e150. Value + time validated BEFORE any state write.
- addFrom(buf, i) -> this        HOT, 0 B/op ZERO-BOX stride-2: now = buf[i], value = buf[i+1] read
                                 UNBOXED. EXPLICIT-time only. Same validation + body (duplicated) as add.
- advance(now) -> this           Move the reference time to `now` WITHOUT adding a value (R11 idle-slide,
                                 ADR 0009): rotate + clear stale panes via the private _advance so an idle
                                 window slides to empty. EXPLICIT-time ONLY, monotone; bounded, 0 B/op.
- advanceFrom(buf, i) -> this    The ZERO-BOX sibling of advance(now): now = buf[i] read UNBOXED (needs
                                 `i < buf.length`), same rotate body, EXPLICIT-only.
- count(w?) -> number            COLD, O(B+1). EXACT count over the covered span (0 on empty; NaN on a bad
                                 w in (0, W]). Boxes once (up to 16 B/call; up to 32 B at a megamorphic
                                 site).
- sum(w?) -> number              COLD, O(B+1). Neumaier-merged windowed sum (0 on empty; NaN on a bad w).
- mean(w?) -> number             COLD, O(B+1). sum / count (NaN on empty; NaN on a bad w).
- min(w?) / max(w?) -> number    COLD, O(B+1). Bit-exact windowed min / max (NaN on empty; NaN on a bad w).
- into(out, w?) -> number        COLD, 0 B/call render path: write `[count, sum, mean, min, max]` into a
                                 caller Float64Array (length >= 5), return 5. NaN slots on a bad w. A
                                 wrong CONTAINER type (a non-Float64Array `out` -> TypeError, out.length
                                 < 5 -> RangeError) throws BEFORE any write. 0 B/call at a monomorphic /
                                 polymorphic site; 16 B/call at a megamorphic site of 5+ subclass shapes.
- clear() -> this                0-alloc reset (reuse both arrays; unlocks the mode).
- W / panes / mode / lastNow / bytes   Getters: the window, the pane count B, the locked mode, the last
                                 applied time, the fixed memory figure ((B+1) * 48; 1584 B at B=32).

Exact-aggregate contract (the honesty anchor, ADR 0012): the witness gates the merged count / sum / mean /
min / max against an EXACT covered-span oracle (BigInt over quantized values) and a true-window lane, plus
a mutation test of `w` for every reader. Negative controls REJECTED by the same gates: a B-pane ring, no
clear on rotate, a dropped straddling pane, Kahan removed, Neumaier removed, empty-pane fill(0) poisoning.
A lite-hud lane (50 lognormal-ms channels) prints next to the EH F17 failure: SlidingAggregate vs its
covered span is EXACT (worst rel 0) where EH vs the true window is 12.7% off. Allocation: torture 0 B/op
with 0 major GC; pinned-probe lanes incl. EVENT-HEAVY rotate-every-add epoch lanes (the 1.8.0 lesson: a
per-event box hides in an average over quiet adds); a +1e12 JumpTiming lane with a per-pane-loop control.

## advance() / idle-slide (ADR 0009)

R11: a sliding-window summary must be able to slide even when NO data arrives. Without it, an
idle stream reports a STALE window -- count()/sum()/quantile() keep returning last-second values
long after the window should have emptied, because the members only expire ON an add(). v1.4.0
adds `advance(now)` / `advanceFrom(buf, i)` to the three TIME-windowed members so the caller can
move the window forward with no traffic.

- advance() moves the window's reference time forward and applies the SAME expiry / rotation an
  add would, WITHOUT inserting a value. Queries stay PURE (they never mutate); advance() is the
  only op that moves the clock without a value.
- Per-member body: ExponentialHistogram runs add()'s expire loop VERBATIM (opens no bucket).
  SlidingHyperLogLog is CLOCK-ONLY (set `_now`; count() skips stamp <= now - W as a PURE read,
  and the next add drops expired heads -- 1.7.0 F8 -- so overflows/degraded never depend on how
  often count() or advance() is called). SlidingDDSketch
  rotates + clears stale panes via the private `_advance` (bounded, <= panes clears).
- Mode rule (all 3, parity with addFrom): EXPLICIT-time ONLY. A COUNT-locked instance throws; an
  UNSET instance locks EXPLICIT (and anchors, for SlidingDDSketch). Monotone: `now` finite and
  >= lastNow (a decrease throws). A rejected advance is a BYTE-IDENTICAL no-op. All 0 B/op.
- EXCLUDED: ForwardDecay (satisfies R11 already via its now? query args -- decay is computed at
  query time relative to `now`, so an idle FD already fades correctly with no advance needed);
  ADWIN, HeavyKeeper, DriftDetector (item-indexed, NOT time-windowed -- they have no `now` axis
  to advance).
- Every existing method + hot body of the three touched classes is BYTE-IDENTICAL; advance /
  advanceFrom are pure additions.

## Query allocation -- the render path (F6)

One rule: a query that RETURNS a fractional or large double boxes ONE ~16 B HeapNumber per call
at a non-inlined call site; the `xxxInto` / `forEach` readers are the 0-alloc render path. So on a
10-15 Hz render loop use `SlidingDDSketch.quantileInto` (0 B/call) not `quantile` (16 B/call), and
`HeavyKeeper.forEach` / `topKInto` (0 B/call) not `topK`. `SlidingCountMin.estimate` boxes 16 B/call
only when the windowed count is >= 2^31 (a Smi-range count returns 0 B/call; `estimateInto` is the
0-alloc batch reader that fixes it), and `SlidingCountMin.total` boxes 16 B/call once the windowed N is
>= 2^31 at a non-inlined site (`totalInto` writes it into a caller slot, 0 B/call). A FRACTIONAL sub-window
`w` is itself a boxed argument at a non-inlined site (16 B/call: `countInto(out, 62.5)` at default flags,
`totalInto(out, 62.5)` under --no-turbo-inlining); the reader 0 B/call figures assume `w` omitted or
integral. `ExponentialHistogram.sum()` and `HeavyKeeper.estimate` box only in
the early JIT tier (steady state 0). `count()` and integer-count returns are Smis, 0 B/call.

## Container arguments -- the HOT / COLD threat model (H2-4, 1.10.0; type-tag hardened, 1.11.0)

The two halves differ on BOTH the type check and the LENGTH read. A HOT entry point (addFrom /
advanceFrom, per item) verifies the type with `ArrayBuffer.isView(x) && x instanceof Float64Array` (a Proxy
passes instanceof alone but not isView) and reads `x.length` ONCE into the index bound -- a caller-defined
subclass length getter may run at most once per call (the caller's own code; the zero-GC hot path is the
product). A COLD render reader (countInto / totalInto / into / estimateInto / quantileInto / topKInto / sampleInto)
instead checks the INTRINSIC type tag -- `TA_TAG.call(x) === 'Float64Array'`, TA_TAG the
%TypedArray%.prototype[@@toStringTag] getter captured at module init, which reads the element-kind of the
internal slot and returns 'Float64Array' ONLY for a genuine Float64Array, undefined (never a throw) for a
prototype-swapped typed array / DataView / Proxy / plain object / primitive, running NO user code -- and
reads the length through the intrinsic %TypedArray%.prototype.length getter (TA_LEN, captured at module
init). So a lying or re-entrant length is ignored and never runs, a benign subclass over a valid backing is
accepted with correct results, and (the 1.11.0 change, S2 RE-SETTLED) a prototype-swapped Uint8Array /
DataView re-parented to Float64Array.prototype is now REJECTED with the tagged TypeError -- before, it was
accepted with silent byte truncation, or hit a native error. A behavior change on invalid input only; a
valid Float64Array behaves byte-identically. Reject messages use a cold describeArg(x) (typeof + isView,
never a trap; String only on a primitive), so a rejected call runs no caller code and mutates nothing (H2-6,
~125 sites).

## The time source + the bucket pool (ADR 0001)

A caller-supplied MONOTONE `now` (logical tick or ms; count-mode convenience when
omitted); the member never reads the wall clock (deterministic, testable). A fixed,
preallocated bucket pool over a Struct-of-Arrays (Float64 timestamp / earliest-time /
size, Int32 per-level linkage + free-list) with no per-op allocation -- the lite-o1
fixed-capacity zero-GC discipline on the recency axis. ADR 0002 records the EH merge /
expire / query + the error bound + the DGIM note + the mode-lock; ADR 0003 the ADWIN2
variance-aware cut + the adaptive shrink; ADR 0004 the ForwardDecay landmark rebase
(exact modulo FP), the FD_EXP_CAP=40 bounded-accumulator + fail-closed-query argument, the signed-value call, and the
rate()=count*lambda definition. ForwardDecay keeps NO pool (two scalar accumulators).

## Scripts

- npm test          -- node:test behavioral + fail-closed suite
- npm run witness   -- the recency witness (windowed error vs the epsilon bound + negative control)
- npm run torture   -- the 0 B/op leak + GC-profiler gate on add incl. reshaping (node --expose-gc)
- npm run test:perf -- flat-throughput perf gate + a must-allocate control
- npm run test:types-- the ambient type-surface compile check
- npm run verify    -- test + test:types + torture + witness + test:perf (the release gate)

## Roadmap

ExponentialHistogram (0.1.0, sliding-window count / sum) -> ADWIN (0.2.0, drift +
adaptive window) -> ForwardDecay (0.3.0, time-decayed aggregates) -> HeavyKeeper
(0.4.0, decayed / windowed heavy hitters) -> 1.0.0 (API freeze -- the four-member roster
is COMPLETE, no new member; a docs / stability milestone) -> 1.1.0 (SlidingHyperLogLog --
windowed distinct-count; the FIRST additive post-1.0 member, a PURE APPEND) -> 1.2.0 (DriftDetector
-- scalar Page-Hinkley / CUSUM change detection; the SECOND additive post-1.0 member, a PURE APPEND)
-> 1.3.0 (SlidingDDSketch -- windowed relative-error quantiles; the THIRD additive post-1.0 member, a
PURE APPEND) -> 1.4.0 (the R11 advance() / advanceFrom() idle-slide sweep on the three TIME-windowed
members -- ExponentialHistogram, SlidingHyperLogLog, SlidingDDSketch; additive, existing methods
byte-identical) -> 1.5.0 (SlidingCountMin -- windowed per-label frequency; the FOURTH additive post-1.0
member, a PURE APPEND) -> 1.6.0 (DecayedReservoir -- recency-biased fixed-k sample; the FIFTH additive
post-1.0 member, a PURE APPEND) -> 1.7.0 (the H1 HARDENING release: in-place fixes across members
from the 1.6.0 final-sweep audit -- NOT a pure append; see CHANGELOG 1.7.0). The 1.6.0 member
COMPLETES the confirmed post-1.0 roadmap. The one remaining
optional / unscheduled tail member is an error-rate DDM / EDDM detector (Bernoulli error-bit stream ->
stable / warning / drift) -- built on demand if a consumer asks; it would be a pure append that keeps
the frozen core byte-identical.
